questions.q: Who is the protagonist of "Navlik Nasonkal" and what is his primary occupation?
questions.a: The protagonist is Lahko (लहको), a young sweeper (xaxkth) who works at the railway station. A wrong answer (e.g., naming Yashoda or Ukha) reveals the student hasn't identified the central character around whom the narrative revolves.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why Lahko considers sweeping not just a job but his life (थोडक व जीवन).
questions.a: Lahko sees sweeping as his identity and source of dignity; he takes pride in doing it thoroughly, as shown when he cleans the platform meticulously even when unwell. A wrong answer that treats it as mere economic necessity misses the thematic point that labor can be a source of self-worth.

questions.q: Find two instances in the text where Lahko shows compassion toward others despite his own hardships. Quote the relevant lines (paraphrased) and explain what they reveal.
questions.a: 1. When he gives his own blanket to the shivering old woman (ealk nsoh) on the platform. 2. When he shares his meager food with the hungry children at the tea stall. These show his empathy transcends his poverty. A wrong answer that cites only one instance or misattributes the action indicates superficial reading.

questions.q: Compare Lahko's reaction to the station master's offer of a blanket with Yashoda's reaction to the same situation. What does this contrast reveal about their characters?
questions.a: Lahko refuses the blanket out of self-respect, saying he doesn't need charity, while Yashoda accepts it gratefully. This contrast highlights Lahko's fierce dignity versus Yashoda's pragmatic acceptance of help. A wrong answer that sees both as similar misses the nuance of Lahko's pride.

questions.q: Evaluate whether Lahko's dream of educating himself and escaping his circumstances is portrayed as realistic or idealistic by the author. Support your judgment with textual evidence.
questions.a: The author portrays it as idealistic yet deeply human; Lahko's attempts to learn (asking about Delhi, trying to read) are shown against overwhelming systemic barriers (illiteracy, caste, poverty), making his hope poignant but fragile. A wrong answer that calls it purely realistic ignores the structural obstacles the text emphasizes.

questions.q: Write a diary entry from Lahko's perspective on the night he meets the old woman (ealk nsoh), capturing his inner conflict between pride and compassion.
questions.a: A good entry will show Lahko's voice: simple language, sensory details of the cold platform, his hesitation to give his only blanket, and his ultimate decision driven by humanity. A poor entry will sound like a generic student essay, lacking Lahko's specific vocabulary and emotional texture.
